HOME AND DAILY LIFE LESSON · HOME AND DAILY LIFE · AGES 3–5 YEARS

Safe at Home — a step-by-step lesson for grown-up and child

This lesson teaches safety as geography: the child learns where the safe things live, because knowing where safety lives is the first skill of being safe.

What is this?

The safe-at-home team: the first-aid box for bumps, the helmet for wheels, the key up high, the light switch, and the handwash at every sink.

What does it mean?

Safety tours done calmly make safety ordinary. A child who has peeked inside the first-aid box on a normal Tuesday is not frightened of it on the day it is needed.

What does the child need to know?

You need the card and the real locations: the first-aid box, the helmet, the sinks. Nothing is opened in an emergency mood — this is a tour, not a drill.

Why this matters

The kit-box pair rides here too — box in the UK, kit in the US, the same brave little container. And the keys rule comes attached: grown-up treasure, up high, never play.

What it teaches

Location memory (where does safety live?), hygiene habits (handwash at every sink), and the calm-fact tone that keeps safety from becoming scary.

Words to learn

first-aid boxfirst-aid kithelmetkeylight switchhandwash

Say this to your child

“"Safe at home — the guardians! The first-aid box waits for bumps, the helmet waits for wheels, the handwash waits at every sink. You know where safety lives now."”

Step by step

  1. Show the card: "our home has guardians — let us visit them all."
  2. The first-aid box: open it together — plasters, cream, the family phone list. Say where it lives and put it back.
  3. The helmet: try it on — helmets go on before wheels, bikes and scooters alike.
  4. The handwash: one pump at the real sink — where it lives, when we use it.
  5. The light switch and the key: lights off when we leave a room; keys up high, grown-up treasure.

Look closer at the picture

On this card the words "Safe at Home" sit over a first-aid box with a red cross, a cycling helmet, a single key, a light switch on its plate and a round green handwash bottle.

Ask your child

"Where does the first-aid box live?" (say your real spot) "When does the helmet go on?" (before wheels) "Whose job is the key?" (the grown-ups&rsquo; — up high)

What your child can say or do

Your child might parade in the helmet all afternoon, restock the first-aid box like a nurse, or switch off every light in empty rooms with great authority.

Out in the real world

The same guardians stand watch in every home you visit — ask your hosts where the first-aid box lives. Knowing to ask is half the lesson already learned.

Try it together

Guardian Tour: draw the house as a simple map, and the child marks X on each guardian&rsquo;s home — first-aid box, helmet, handwash sinks. The map goes on the fridge; safety has addresses now.

Understanding check

Ask: "What do we put on before wheels?" (the helmet) "Where does the key stay?" (up high — grown-up treasure) "What do we do at the sink?" (handwash)

This lesson pairs with the Safe at Home flashcard in the library — print it, show it, keep it on the fridge. Back to Home and Daily Life.
